description:
Schema-only envelope for the complete HTTP/WebSocket surface. It is never
serialized on the wire; it exists so one root schema can reference every
versioned HTTP DTO from the same Rust definitions used at runtime.
title: NodeHttpContract

NodeCommandHttpRequest.description:
Versioned request DTO for `POST /api/node/commands`.

The embedded `NodeCommandRequest` is forwarded unchanged to
`NodeCommandBus`; the adapter does not inspect or mutate node state.

NodeCommandRequest.description: One request accepted by the node command layer from CLI, IPC, WebUI or GPUI.

oneOf.description:
Bootstrap query for the declarative UI contract. This is not rendered as
a page action and should be called before an adapter builds its UI.

NodeCommand.description:
Product-neutral node operations. A node creates, joins or serves a network;
there are deliberately no product-level client/server command variants.

oneOf.description: Keep the node and its control surfaces running without joining a network.

NodeNetworkSelection.description: How a node should choose the networks it loads at startup.

NodeNetworkRole.description: Network roles are capabilities within a network, never product identities.

NodeCommandHttpResponse.description:
Versioned response DTO containing the exact result returned by the command
bus. Rejected results remain visible in the body alongside their HTTP status.

exit_node_capabilities.description:
Runtime capability truth for this host. Adapters must disable Exit Node
actions when `supported` is false and render the typed reasons instead
of inferring success from configuration alone.

capabilities.description:
Unified four-capability projection shared by every UI adapter. Missing
entries deserialize as `Unknown`; they are never inferred as enabled.

NodeSnapshot.description: Stable, transport-neutral state rendered by every node UI adapter.

NodeLifecycleSnapshot.description: Shared lifecycle snapshot consumed by CLI, IPC, WebUI, and (later) GPUI.

NodePhase.description:
Node-global lifecycle. Network sessions may come and go while the node
remains in one of these phases.

NodeIdentitySnapshot.description: Public node identity metadata. Secret key material must never enter this DTO.

NodeConfigurationSnapshot.description: Effective, non-secret network configuration exposed to every UI adapter.

NodeNetworkConfigSnapshot.description:
One network's effective configuration after loading startup overrides.

Filesystem paths and other host-local details are deliberately omitted. The
boolean fields only state whether optional host-local settings are present.

oneOf.description: 仅使用 IPv4 虚拟内网
仅使用 IPv6 虚拟内网
同时支持 IPv4 和 IPv6 虚拟双栈

ExitNodeCapabilities.description:
Current, non-secret Exit Node capability truth for one node process.

`supported` describes whether a basic IPv4 Exit Node can be installed now.
`ipv6_forwarding` is independent because an IPv6-only limitation does not
make the IPv4 Exit Node implementation unusable.

ExitNodePlatform.description: Host platforms with distinct Exit Node implementation requirements.

ExitNodeUnsupportedReason.description:
Machine-readable reasons that make an Exit Node action unavailable.

Adapters must render these reasons instead of treating an enabled config
flag as proof that kernel forwarding and NAT were installed.

NodeCapabilityRegistrySnapshot.description:
Stable projection of the fixed first-version capability set. Unknown
entries fail closed and unsupported capabilities remain visible so the UI
can explain why an action is unavailable.

CapabilityKind.description:
The fixed first-version capability set. Unknown wire values fail closed at
deserialization and are never inferred from a free-form label.

oneOf.description:
A migrated record may preserve an unreadable state without making the
capability usable. New writes may not create this state.

NodePermissionSnapshot.description:
Control-plane authorization posture shared with UI adapters.

`TrustedControlPlane` means the runtime accepts every connected adapter as
fully privileged. It does not mean per-user or remote authentication exists.

NodePermission.description: Stable capability classes used by both the permission snapshot and UI actions.

NodeEmbeddedServiceSnapshot.description:
Non-secret runtime state for one network's embedded signaling and relay
services. Invitation tickets, identity material, and host-local paths are
deliberately excluded from this shared UI contract.

UiMode.description:
The actual control surface selected for this node process.

`WebUi` is the browser-hosted control plane. It remains available on
headless hosts as a server-only surface; the display environment only
decides whether a browser window can also be opened. `WebUi` must never be
represented as the native `Gpui` surface.

NodeNetworkSnapshot.description: One local network and the roles this node currently performs in it.

NodePeerSnapshot.description: Peer state scoped to a network. The same node may appear in multiple networks.

NodeProblem.description: UI- and transport-neutral error returned by every node command adapter.

oneOf.description: The operation is valid but unavailable on this platform or host.

NodeUiManifest.description:
Declarative contract shared by WebUI and the future native GPUI surface.

Adapters may choose different widgets and rendering, but page availability,
commands, fields, validation, confirmations, permission classes and backend
maturity come from this manifest rather than duplicated UI business logic.

audit.description:
Stable audit requirement for this command. Reads that are too noisy to
record still carry an explicit `none` declaration instead of leaving
adapters to guess.

oneOf.description: The production command handler currently accepts this command.
The shared command exists, but the runtime backend rejects it as unavailable.

action.description: Stable action name written to the append-only audit log.

NodeManifestResponse.description: Versioned DTO returned by the UI-manifest endpoint.

NodeSnapshotResponse.description: Versioned DTO returned by the snapshot endpoint.

NodeHttpErrorResponse.description:
Versioned HTTP error DTO. It is also used for WebSocket version mismatches
so clients receive a machine-readable failure before an upgrade.

NodeHttpErrorCode.description: Stable error codes for HTTP version negotiation and backend failures.

NodeWsMessage.description:
Versioned WebSocket messages. A snapshot is sent immediately after upgrade;
every later state or operational event carries the same adapter version.

NodeEvent.description: Ordered event delivered to every attached UI and control adapter.

oneOf.description: The broadcast receiver fell behind and lost one or more events.
Event revisions skipped values, so incremental application is unsafe.

NodeWsResyncReason.description: Why the server replaced the event stream with a fresh canonical snapshot.
